statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 14 of 100 in the low band, eleven points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 82 and confidence high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ trades 29,291.75-29,292.75, up about 0.54%, after extending the session high to 29,334.00 and retracing roughly forty points, while VIX falls 3.25% to a session-low 17.26, the 10-year holds 4.947% and Brent corrects 2.60% to $104.83, leaving tail at 14 and stress extreme at 82 into the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report.
body:
The new evidence this hour is a genuine extension of the overnight advance. NQ trades 29,291.75 on one feed and 29,292.75 on a second, up about 0.54% against a 29,135.25 previous close, after printing a fresh session high of 29,334.00 on both. That high sits roughly sixty-two points above the 29,272.00 top recorded an hour ago, so the session extreme was taken out rather than merely retested. Against the 29,040.50 overnight low the band has widened to about 293 points, and price currently sits some forty points beneath the high.

Holding near a session extreme after a new high is the one genuine tail amplifier present, and it is why tail moves from 13 to 14 rather than lower. It stops there because the amplifier is isolated and because the retracement now underway is the widest of the session. The structure that defines tail risk is repeated extension after failed retracements; what is observable instead is one new high followed by a forty-point giveback, which is the ordinary two-way behaviour of a trending but orderly session.

The cross-asset picture argues the same way and has continued to ease. VIX is 17.26, down 3.25%, having printed a session low of 17.12 inside a 17.12 to 17.71 band. A volatility index making session lows while the index makes session highs is the signature of an orderly drift, not of the violent directional repricing tail is meant to capture. The ten-year yield is 4.947%, essentially unchanged on the day and comfortably below the 4.978% peak set in early Asian trading, after Reuters reported it reaching 4.97% overnight, the highest since late 2023. The two-year is 4.558%, up under a basis point and below its own 4.583% high. Brent has corrected 2.60% to $104.83 and WTI 2.16% to $100.26, having reached a four-month high near $109.97 on course for a weekly gain of roughly 13%. Oil retreating is a direct reduction in the inflation impulse driving the whole rate-hike narrative, so none of the three main cross-asset channels is aligned behind an equity melt-up.

Stress stays extreme but eases a point to 82 on that same oil and volatility correction. The backdrop is unchanged in substance: a global bond selloff has carried the ten-year toward 5% with borrowing costs at multi-decade highs from Tokyo to London, crude has held above $100 on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz shipping conflict, the European Central Bank raised rates on Thursday and warned that price pressures could prove lasting, and the STOXX 600 is up 0.4% at 638.63 while heading for its sharpest weekly decline in about two months. Market pricing puts the probability of a Federal Reserve increase on 16 September at roughly 67% to 72% depending on the source and time of day, up from 49% a week earlier. That is precisely the difficult, high-volatility environment stress is built to describe, and under this framework it is scored separately from the price-path question.

One sector-level input is worth naming because it cuts against the Thursday cash tape. TSMC reported August revenue of NT$514.81 billion, up 10.1% on the month and 53.3% on the year, a record month and a fourth consecutive monthly increase driven by artificial-intelligence demand. Thursday's U.S. semiconductor session was broadly negative, so the overnight bid in Nasdaq futures is being supported by a catalyst the last cash close did not reflect.

The August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC is the final inflation input before the decision, with consensus near 3.3% to 3.4% headline year-on-year and 2.4% to 2.5% core. It is a checkpoint, not an automatic block: its importance and the dispersion around it are scored in stress and confidence, and tail will be revised on the observed post-release path rather than on the size of any surprise. The conditional forecast therefore peaks at 23 in the release slot and 22 across the cash open, both inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, then decays through the afternoon on the assumption that retracements continue to be granted.

Confidence holds at 89. Live NQ quotes are available from two independent feeds, real-time VIX and two-year and ten-year yields are current, oil is current, the seven-day calendar is verified against a primary calendar source, and every material overnight story has been confirmed against reputable reporting. The shared cross-asset context file was both outside its freshness window and flagged as a partial collection at this assessment time, so it was not used; the assessment rests entirely on independently fetched live evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 09:00 UTC on 10 September to 08:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 10 and 11 with the mode recorded as mixed through the European morning. The single excursion sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open with the mode back to trend-down. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to WATCH and neither reached the 25 block threshold. Tail then decayed as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close. From 22:00 UTC the overnight session normalised into an 11 to 15 band with mixed conditions, and the final three slots at 06:00, 07:00 and 08:00 UTC record trend-up at tail 13, 14 and 13 as the overnight advance extended and then pulled back. Stress never left the extreme band, running 82 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence held 84 to 89 throughout.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the rest of the 11 September session and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail starts at 14 on the observed new session high and the wide retracement from it, holds 14 through the European morning and edges to 15 as quoted depth conditionally thins ahead of the release. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open where a post-event move is either confirmed or rejected. The 14:00 UTC slot carrying the preliminary Michigan release eases to 19 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly by then. The afternoon decays through 17, 15 and 14, lifts to 15 into the final pre-close hour and 18 across the 20:00 UTC cash close where weekly positioning concentrates, then falls to a 5 to 7 floor for the closure hours that represents residual gap risk into the Sunday reopen rather than any intraday mechanism. Two slots are mapped to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold. Stress stays extreme through the U.S. session, peaking at 92 in the release slot, and decays into the elevated band across the weekend. Confidence eases from 89 to around 70 as the horizon moves past the last observable quote.
